intro: Fully funded PhD and research-master’s scholarship at NUS: full tuition subsidy plus SGD 3,000/month for international PhD students, with up to SGD 500/month extra after the qualifying exam.
description:
Overview

The NUS Research Scholarship is awarded to outstanding full-time graduate research students at the National University of Singapore. It covers tuition and pays a monthly stipend to international, Singapore-citizen and Singapore-permanent-resident scholars pursuing a PhD or a research master’s degree.

Scholarship consideration is requested inside the NUS admission application — there is no separate scholarship form. Faculty deadlines vary, and the Business School closes earlier than many others, so always check your department’s date.

Stipend and Tuition Coverage

NUS Research Scholarship rates (effective 1 January 2026, verified on official NUS pages)
ItemDetails
International PhD studentSGD 3,000 per month, plus full tuition subsidy.
International research master’s studentSGD 2,900 per month, plus full tuition subsidy.
Singapore permanent resident (PhD / research master’s)SGD 3,400 / SGD 3,000 per month.
Singapore citizen (PhD / research master’s)SGD 3,800 per month, plus CPF contributions.
PhD qualifying exam supplementUp to an additional SGD 500 per month after passing the qualifying examination, reviewed each semester and limited to the 48th month of candidature for applicable cohorts.
President’s Graduate Fellowship (PGF)Outstanding students may be recommended for the PGF, which carries a higher stipend (around SGD 3,900/month is mentioned in departmental material).
DurationInitially one year, renewed semester by semester on progress; maximum four years for a PhD and two years for a research master’s.
Not coveredMandatory miscellaneous student fees (registration, student activity, health service, insurance, academic-related), housing, flights and other living costs. Applicable fees may be deducted from the stipend at the start of each semester.

Eligibility

  • Outstanding graduates of any nationality applying to a full-time NUS graduate research programme (PhD or Master’s by Research).
  • Published academic threshold: an undergraduate qualification at the level of Second Class Honours (Upper Division), Honours (Distinction) or equivalent. Provide an official grading scale if your transcript uses a different system.
  • English-test requirements follow NUS admission rules (TOEFL/IELTS); some departments may waive GRE and TOEFL for exceptional candidates.
  • Faculty and school deadlines vary — the College of Design and Engineering (CDE) lists 15 January 2027 for international candidates.

Application Timeline

Illustrative August 2027 intake deadlines (faculty-specific — verify your own)
ItemDetails

CDE — Singapore-resident scholarship applicantsRound 1: 15 January 2027; Round 2: 1 March 2027 (funding permitting).
NUS Business School PhDApplications from 1 May 2026 to 15 December 2026.
Statistics & Data Science PhD16 May to 15 November 2026; formal acceptance notifications in January 2027.
Saw Swee Hock School of Public HealthCloses 1 November 2026; transcripts and referee reports by 15 November 2026.

How to Apply

  • Choose your research degree, department and intake, and confirm the current checklist in the NUS GradApp portal.
  • Prepare transcripts, degree records, CV, statement of purpose, research material, references and English-test results as directed by your department.
  • Complete the admission application and indicate that you want to be considered for the NUS Research Scholarship where the portal asks about funding.
  • Review admission and funding decisions separately — an admission offer alone does not establish that funding was awarded. Read the written funding offer before committing.

Official Link

NUS Graduate School — NUS Research Scholarship

Important Notes

  • NUS does not set one central deadline: verify the date on your faculty’s website, especially for the Business School.
  • Singapore living costs are high — budget housing and arrival expenses from your stipend, and note that first-stipend payments may lag.
  • The 15 January 2027 date is the CDE international reference deadline; other faculties may differ.
